text:
You are the video agent of an explainer channel. You build ONE chapter of a narrated lesson as a finished video, in
Manim Community (Python), by yourself, end to end: you decide what is on screen, how it moves and how it looks. There
are no templates, primitives or layouts to use: you write the scene from nothing, as a motion designer who codes.

WHAT YOU HAVE
- The narration: the chapter is already spoken. timing.json in your workspace has every line with its start and end,
  and every word with its own, in seconds on the chapter's track (chapter.wav); they are also below. The video is built
  to the voice: it lasts as long as the narration, and each thing appears or changes on the words that name it.
- narrated.py (in your workspace): `from narrated import NarratedScene`. Subclass it as `class Chapter(NarratedScene)`
  in scene.py. It adds the voice to the scene and tells you the time; nothing else:
    self.now                          seconds into the chapter so far
    self.line(n)                      line n (0-based): {text, start, end, words: [{w, start, end}]}
    self.word(n, "Japan", occurrence=0) when that word is said in line n (matched by its start, case aside)
    self.phrase(n, "string of islands") when that run of words begins in line n
    self.wait_until(t, lead=0.0)       hold until lead seconds before t (nothing if passed)
    self.wait_until_end()              hold to the end of the narration; call it last
  Plays take their run_time; between them, wait_until the next word. Start an animation a little before its word
  (lead 0.1-0.3) so it lands as the word is said.
- A screenshot of the look wanted (attached: a Vox-like explainer). Match its feel: its palette, type,
  textures, how labels and highlights look, how busy a frame is. It is a look, not a layout: compose each moment yourself.
- Tools to write and edit files, render, look at frames, make pictures, run commands, and check the phone.

THE ONE HARD RULE: THE PHONE
The video is not shipped as an MP4. The phone (and the web player) play the scene as a program recorded from Manim, and
it must look exactly as Manim drew it. Every play is recorded as Manim draws it, frame by frame, so almost anything
Manim does plays, with these limits:
- 2D: anything goes, camera moves included (mix MovingCameraScene into your class with NarratedScene to zoom and
  pan with self.camera.frame). 3D (ThreeDScene) is only partly supported on the phone: see-through solids lose faces
  and the web player cannot preview it; prefer 2D.
- Pictures (PNG, JPG) as ImageMobject are fine. Load files by absolute path: Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "assets" / ...
- Size: every frame of motion costs bytes; a still hold costs nothing. Keep the program under about 20 MB for the
  chapter (phone_check says its size): no endless idle motion, no updaters ticking through long holds, no needless
  points (simplify map outlines).
- phone_check must pass before you finish: it exports the scene and compares the phone's frames with the render's.

HOW TO WORK (as a careful engineer works)
1. Read the narration. Write plan.md: the chapter's moments, each with its lines and times, what is on screen and
   which words drive what. One clear idea on screen at a time; something meaningful changes every few seconds.
2. Build scene.py in pieces you can check: render a draft early, look at a sheet of frames, then frames at the
   moments that matter (where things land on words, where text could overlap or leave the frame). Fix what you see.
   Look before you believe: a frame shows overlaps, cut-off text, unreadable sizes and empty screens that code hides.
3. The frame is x -7.1..7.1, y -4..4 (16:9). Keep everything inside with a margin; text at least font_size 24.
   Fonts: use what is installed (shell: fc-list); the narration may be in Hindi or Hinglish: Devanagari needs a font
   that has it (Noto Sans Devanagari, Hind). Subtitles are your choice.
4. When it is right, render final, run phone_check, and finish. If the phone differs, find why (an unsupported
   feature, a camera move) and change the scene.
You have at most 60 turns: plan, then build steadily; do not stop at a first draft that you have not looked at.
Every tool call is a turn. Say briefly what you are doing and why as you go.
मैं पहले narration के साथ दृश्य-योजना और नक्शों की तैयारी करूँगा, फिर पूरा chapter बनाकर उसके timing और phone playback की जाँच करूँगा।

    from narrated import NarratedScene

    class Chapter(NarratedScene):
        def construct(self):
            self.wait_until(self.word(0, "Japan"))     # hold until "Japan" in line 0 is said
            self.play(FadeIn(japan))

            self.wait_until_end()                      # hold to the end of the narration

the Manim video and the phone's program both carry the voice. With no timing file the scene still runs, silent,

def _norm(word: str) -> str:
    """A word as compared: lower case, accents off Latin letters (an Indian script's signs kept), no punctuation."""
    out = []
    for ch in unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", word.lower()):
        if unicodedata.category(ch) == "Mn" and ord(ch) < 0x0900:
            continue
        if ch.isalnum() or unicodedata.category(ch) in ("Mn", "Mc"):
            out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out)


def load(folder: Path = HERE) -> dict:
    """The chapter's timing: {"seconds", "lines": [{"n", "text", "start", "end", "words": [{"w", "start", "end"}]}]}."""
    path = folder / "timing.json"
    if path.is_file():
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if data.get("lines"):
            return data
    lines = []
    script = folder / "lines.json"
    texts = json.loads(script.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["lines"] if script.is_file() else []
    clock = 0.0
    for n, text in enumerate(texts):
        words = text.split()
        row = {"n": n, "text": text, "start": clock, "words": []}
        for w in words:
            row["words"].append({"w": w, "start": clock, "end": clock + 0.42})
            clock += 0.42

        clock += 0.3
        lines.append(row)
    return {"seconds": clock, "lines": lines, "track": None}

# Chapter 3 — दो पड़ोसी, अलग जमीन (229.7 s)

Visual language: warm paper grain, charcoal ink, vermilion map highlights, mustard underlines, olive terrain, blue rivers; Oswald English headings / Kohinoor Devanagari Hindi. Full-frame editorial compositions, not a slide grid. Persistent small chapter folio. Geographic outlines from Natural Earth, simplified. All overlays timed to spoken nouns; holds are static.

0–14 | lines 0–2: title and paired China/Japan silhouettes. Geography cue strip (mountains, plains, rain, sea), then East Asian locator.
14–40 | lines 3–6: large China map, terrain triangles and climatic band cues. Three river paths revealed at their names, Yangtse third-longest callout. Takeaway: varied land → varied lives.
40–63 | lines 7–10: China outline remains left; people/language editorial blocks on right. Han, Putonghua, then Uighur/Hui/Manchu/Tibetan; Cantonese=Yue and Shanghainese=Wu. Conclude diversity, not uniformity.
63–88 | lines 11–14: four regional food quadrants; southern/Cantonese selected. Illustrated dim sum platter, diaspora arrow, then literal meaning highlighted.
88–113 | lines 15–18: food geography map: north wheat, east rice+wheat, Szechuan red. Silk Route spices and maritime chili arrows enter Szechuan; date explicitly attributed to book.
113–133 | lines 19–21: Japan close-up geographic map; sequential leader labels Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu. Okinawa to south, Bahamas latitude comparison in sidebar.
133–151 | lines 22–24: mountainous Japan + 50%+ bar, earthquake rings. House diagram replaces sidebar, geography → architecture headline.
151–166 | lines 25–26: population graphic, Ainu/Hokkaido highlight; Korea → Japan forced-labour arrow. Colonial coercion explicitly labeled, no voluntary-migration implication.
166–181 | lines 27–28: animal husbandry weak tradition; rice and fish as staples, sashimi/sushi illustrated plate. Avoid implying all sushi is raw fish.
181–205 | lines 29–31: East Asia map with red historical territorial schematic, prominent 1941 date and 'not early 19th century'. Japan, Korea, Manchuria, eastern China highlights in sequence. Taiwan and five city markers at named words.
205–225 | lines 32–33: same map with sea labels, trade connections. Wider regional context shows Russia/Mongolia/Kazakhstan/India.
225–229.7 | line 34: simplify to Japan and closing question 'असल सत्ता किसके पास?' for next chapter.

Engineering: no idle updaters, short reveals, map paths simplified. Render draft, inspect sheets and dense labels, final render + phone_check required.

from manim import *
from narrated import NarratedScene
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np, json

A=Path(__file__).resolve().parent/'assets'
INK='#252623'; PAPER='#E3DDCB'; RED='#D94142'; YELLOW='#F4CE45'; OLIVE='#899565'; BLUE='#397D8C'; LAND='#D5C6A3'; WHITE='#F7F4E9'
DATA=json.loads((A/'maps.json').read_text())

def txt(s,size=30,color=INK,font=None):
    return Text(s,font=font or ('Kohinoor Devanagari' if any('\u0900'<=c<='\u097f' for c in s) else 'Avenir Next'),font_size=size,color=color)
def tag(s,p,size=26,fill=WHITE,color=INK):
    t=txt(s,size,color); b=Rectangle(width=t.width+.24,height=t.height+.18,stroke_color=INK,stroke_width=1.2,fill_color=fill,fill_opacity=1)
    return VGroup(b,t).move_to(p)
def label(s,p,size=30,color=INK): return txt(s,size,color).move_to(p)
def path(points,color=BLUE,width=4):
    v=VMobject().set_points_as_corners(points); v.set_stroke(color,width); return v
def mountain(p,s=.16):
    return Polygon(np.array(p)+[-s,-s*.65,0],np.array(p)+[0,s,0],np.array(p)+[s,-s*.65,0],stroke_color=INK,stroke_width=.8,fill_color=OLIVE,fill_opacity=1)
class Geo:
    def __init__(self,bounds,rect):
        self.lo,self.la,self.hi,self.ha=bounds; self.x,self.y,self.w,self.h=rect
    def p(self,lon,lat): return np.array([self.x+(lon-self.lo)/(self.hi-self.lo)*self.w,self.y+(lat-self.la)/(self.ha-self.la)*self.h,0])
    def country(self,n,fill=LAND,stroke=INK):
        return VGroup(*[Polygon(*[self.p(*c) for c in ring],stroke_color=stroke,stroke_width=.85,fill_color=fill,fill_opacity=1) for ring in DATA[n]])
    def region(self,pts,fill=RED): return Polygon(*[self.p(*p) for p in pts],stroke_color=RED,stroke_width=2,fill_color=fill,fill_opacity=.55)
    def river(self,pts): return path([self.p(*p) for p in pts],BLUE,4)

class Chapter(NarratedScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.bg=ImageMobject(str(A/'paper.png')).set(width=14.23,height=8)
        self.add(self.bg)
        self.folio=label('03   /   दो पड़ोसी, अलग जमीन',[-4.75,3.67,0],24)
        self.add(self.folio,Line([-6.6,3.35,0],[6.6,3.35,0],color=INK,stroke_width=1))
        self.base=list(self.mobjects)
        def at(t,*an,rt=.5):
            self.wait_until(t,lead=.15); self.play(*an,run_time=rt)
        def show(t,m,rt=.5): at(t,FadeIn(m,shift=UP*.08),rt=rt); return m
        def wipe(t):
            self.wait_until(t,lead=.15)
            obs=[m for m in self.mobjects if m not in self.base]
            if obs:self.play(*[FadeOut(m) for m in obs],run_time=.35)
        def head(s): return label(s,[0,2.8,0],43,font if False else INK)
        def caption(s,y=-3.25): return tag(s,[0,y,0],28,INK,WHITE)
        def leader(g,coord,s,pos,size=26,fill=WHITE):
            p=g.p(*coord); lab=tag(s,pos,size,fill); end=lab.get_left() if pos[0]>p[0] else lab.get_right()
            return VGroup(Line(p,end,color=INK,stroke_width=1.3),Dot(p,radius=.045,color=INK),lab)
        def china():
            g=Geo((73,18,136,54),(-6.3,-2.6,7.6,5.1));return g,g.country('China',WHITE)
        def japan():
            g=Geo((127,24,147,46),(-5.8,-2.7,6.2,5.7));return g,g.country('Japan',WHITE)
        # Opening: paired landforms
        c=Geo((73,18,136,54),(-5.9,-.5,5,2.9)).country('China',RED)
